slots.title: July housing starts −12.4% MoM, 1.239M
slots.body: July housing starts: **1.239M** (est. **1.35M**, prior **1.415M**). Month-over-month change: **−12.4%** (est. **−4.7%**, prior **+19.7%**). That is the headline housing construction print for July—new ground-breaking slowed much more than economists expected after June’s **19.7%** jump. Building permits, released in the same batch, came in higher on the month; starts are the piece that missed. How much weight do you put on one month of starts versus permits?

slots.title: July permits 1.443M beat 1.37M estimate
slots.body: July building permits: **1.443M** vs **1.37M** expected (prior **1.374M**). Permits month over month: **+5%** vs **+1.2%** expected (prior **−2.6%**). Permits are approvals to build later; starts are when work begins—same morning, opposite signals. Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q3 was also updated today at **4%** vs **4.3%** estimate and prior **4.3%**, a small step down in the Fed’s nowcast. Do permits or starts tell the better story for housing right now?
